<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|300|THE ACTES|CHA. V.}}</noinclude>God, and said, Lord, thou that didst make heauen & earth, the sea, and al things that are in them, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}}† vvho in the holy Ghost by the mouth of our father Dauid thy seruant hast said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 2, 1.''}}* ''VVhy did the Gentiles rage, and the people meditate vaine thinges'': {{verse|chapter=4|verse=26}}† ''the kings of the earth stand vp, and the Princes assemble together against our Lord, and against his Christ?''

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=27}}† For there assembled in deede in this citie against thy holy childe {{sc|Iesvs}} vvhom thou hast anointed, Herod, and Pontius Pilate, vvith the Gentiles and the people of Israël, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=28}}† to doe vvhat {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christes death, as needeful for mans redemption, was of Gods determination: but as of the malice of the Ievves, it vvas not his act othervvise then by permission.}}∷ thy hand & thy counsel decreed to be done. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=29}}† And novv Lord looke vpon their threatenings, and giue vnto thy seruants vvith al confidence to speake thy vvorde, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=30}}† in that, that thou extend thy hand to cures and signes and vvonders to be done by the name of thy holy sonne {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=31}}† And vvhen they had praied, the place vvas moued vvherein they vvere gathered: and they vvere al replenished vvith the holy Ghost, and they spake the vvord of God vvith confidence.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=32}}† And the multitude of beleeuers had one hart and one soule: neither did any one say that ought vvas his ovvne of those things vvhich he possessed, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 2, 44.''}}* but al things vvere common vnto them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=33}}† And vvith great povver did the Apostles giue testimonie of the resurrection of {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} our Lord: and great grace vvas in al them. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=34}}† For neither vvas there any one needie among them. For as many as vvere ovvners of landes or houses, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note the ardent charitie and contempt of worldly things in the first Christians: who did not only giue great alms, but}}∷ sold and brought the prices of those things vvhich they sold, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=35}}† and laid it before the feete of the Apostles. And to euery one vvas deuided according as euery one hade neede. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=36}}† And Ioseph vvho vvas surnamed of the Apostles Barnabas (vvhich is by interpretation, the sonne of consolation) a Leuite, a Cyprian borne, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=37}}† vvhereas he had a peece of land, sold it, and brought the price, and laid it {{sup|‖}} before the feete of the Apostles.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IIII.}}}}

''37. Before the feete.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Reuerence to holy persons.}}He, as the rest, did not onely giue his goods as in vulgar almes, but in al humble and reuerent maner as things dedicated to God, he laid them downe at the Apostles holy feete, as S. Luke alwaies expresseth, and gaue them not into their handes. The Sunamite {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''4. reg. 4, 27''.}}fel downe and embraced Elisæus feete. Many that asked benefites of Christ (as the woman sicke of the bloudy fluxe) fel downe at his feete. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 8, 47.''}}and Marie kissed his feete. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Kissing their feete.}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 7, 38.''}}Such are signes of due reuerence done both to Christ and to other sacred persons, either Prophetes, Apostles, Popes, or others representing his person in earth. See in S. Hierom of Epiphanius Bishop in Cypres, how the people of Hierusalem ''of al sortes flocked together vnto him, offering their children'' (to take his blessing) ''kissing his feete, plucking the hemmes of his garment, so that he could not moue for the throng''. Ep. 61 c. 4 cont. erro. Io. Hierosol.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}}}

{{c|''Ananias and his vvife Saphira, for their sacrilege, at Peters word fall downe dead, to the great terrour of the rest. 12 By the Apostles miracles, not onely the number, but also their faith so increaseth, that they seeke in the streates to the very shadow of Peter, the townes also about bringing their diseased to Hierusalem. 17 The Rulers againe oppose them selues, but in vaine. 19 For out of prison an Angel deliuereth them, bidding them preach openly to al: 27 and in their Councel Peter is nothing afraid of their bigge wordes: 34 Yea Gamaliel being one of them selues casteth a doubt among them, lest the matter be of God, and therfore impossible to be dissolued. 40 Finally, the Apostles being scourged by them, count it an honour, and cease no day from preaching.''}} {{dropinitial|B|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial B, heads among foliage.png|imgsize=235px|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}VT a certaine man named Ananias, vvith Saphîra his vvife sold a peece of land, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}}† and {{sup|‖}} defrauded of the price of the land, his vvife being priuie thereto: and bringing a certaine portion, laide it at the feete of the Apostles. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}}† And {{sup|‖}} Peter said, Ananias, vvhy hath Satan tempted thy hart, that thou shouldest lie to the holy<noinclude>{{rh|||Ghost,}}</noinclude>
